thesis: AI is dominated by large pretrained Transformer models, with inference-time reasoning emerging as a second path to greater capability. Chat remains the dominant interface, while agents, multimodality and open-weight models expand what the paradigm can do.

bottlenecks.name: Compute cost and availability
bottlenecks.problem: Frontier training needs tens of thousands of accelerators, and supply is bounded by fabrication, advanced packaging and the electricity a site can obtain.
evidence: NVIDIA Blackwell announced with rack-scale power requirements — 2024-03
CoWoS packaging repeatedly identified as the accelerator supply constraint — 2023/2024

bottlenecks.name: Reliability
bottlenecks.problem: Models remain confidently wrong, errors compound across multi-step work, and the human verification needed to catch them can erase the value of generating anything.

bottlenecks.name: Agency
bottlenecks.problem: Models can call tools but cannot be trusted to carry out long tasks unattended, and nothing exists to make delegated authority accountable.
evidence: Claude computer use released with reliability caveats — 2024-10
EU AI Act entered into force — 2024-08

bottlenecks.name: Closed frontier
bottlenecks.problem: The leading models are API-only and disclose neither their data nor their training method, though capable open weights are now released within months of them.
evidence: GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 released without architecture or data disclosure — 2024
DeepSeek-V3 open weights with published method — 2024-12

bottlenecks.name: Context and memory
bottlenecks.problem: Weights are frozen at training. Context windows are long but nothing accumulates across sessions, so a model never learns from the work it does.
evidence: retrieval remains the standard substitute for memory — 2024

bottlenecks.name: Data quality and supply
bottlenecks.problem: The supply of new high-quality public text is increasingly constrained, while legal access is narrowing through litigation and licensing.
evidence: Will We Run Out of Data?, revised — 2024-06

bottlenecks.name: Inference cost and latency
bottlenecks.problem: Per-token prices have fallen sharply, but the reasoning models that answer hardest questions spend far more compute per answer and are correspondingly slow.
evidence: sustained per-token price declines across providers — 2024

bottlenecks.name: Customization
bottlenecks.problem: Adapting a model to a domain or organisation is easier than it was, but the best models still cannot be fine-tuned at all.
evidence: LoRA and PEFT routine on open models — 2024
fine-tuning unavailable on leading closed models — 2024

layers.paradigm: NVIDIA GPU datacenters dominate frontier training
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires large accelerator clusters, with NVIDIA GPUs as the industry default.
evidence: CoWoS packaging named as the binding supply constraint — 2023/2024

layers.assumption: Transformer attention remains the architecture for frontier models; gains come from sparsity, scale and multimodality rather than from replacing attention.

distribution.basis: architecture family of 8 selected frontier-scale production models released 2023-2024 — GPT-4/4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405B, Grok-2, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen2.5-72B, Mistral Large 2; every publicly described example in this sample is attention-based

layers.paradigm: Large-scale pretraining followed by increasingly capability-enhancing post-training
layers.assumption: Pretraining creates the base model, while post-training can now improve capabilities such as reasoning rather than merely shape behaviour.
frontier: process reward models and step-level supervision
large-scale synthetic and self-generated training data
distillation of reasoning traces into smaller models
evidence: Let's Verify Step by Step (process supervision) — 2023-05
OpenAI o1-preview, RL on reasoning traces — 2024-09
Phi series trained on synthetic textbooks — 2023/2024
post-training methods are inconsistently disclosed and the boundary between preference RL and verifiable-reward RL is not clean — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Web-scale crawl, increasingly licensed, supplemented by large synthetic corpora
layers.assumption: Continued scaling requires increasingly curated, proprietary, licensed or synthetic data as easily accessible high-quality public text becomes constrained.
frontier: synthetic and self-generated data at pretraining scale
evidence: Will We Run Out of Data? Villalobos et al. — 2022, revised 2024-06
New York Times v. OpenAI filed — 2023-12
no defensible share data for this layer — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Capability scales along two compute axes: training-time compute and inference-time reasoning compute
layers.assumption: More compute can improve capability both before deployment through training and during inference through extended reasoning.
frontier: adaptive allocation of inference compute per query
search and parallel sampling over reasoning traces
distillation of long reasoning into short inference
sparse scaling at constant active compute
evidence: reports of diminishing returns from pretraining scale — 2024-11
no public source apportions frontier compute between pretraining and inference — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Long context windows with retrieval; weights frozen after training
layers.assumption: Weights are frozen at training; anything that must persist lives outside the model, in the context window or a retrieval index.
frontier: continual learning and weight updates after deployment
evidence: RAG remains the standard pattern for persistence — 2023/2024
context length is a property of the paradigm, not a share of it — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Conversational multimodal assistants with realtime voice dominate, while agents and IDE-native AI emerge
layers.assumption: The primary end-user interface for general AI is conversational chat.
evidence: Cursor and IDE-native assistants in wide use — 2024
no public source apportions usage across chat, API, IDE and agents — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Frontier development remains concentrated among well-capitalised labs, but capable open-weight models and rapidly falling inference prices broaden access
layers.assumption: Training the best models requires capital and compute available to only a small number of organisations.
frontier: open-weight models at or near frontier capability
small models distilled to frontier-adjacent capability
evidence: DeepSeek-V3, 671B MoE trained for a reported ~$5.6M — 2024-12
